title: Guided Economy Onramp — PRD scratch
content:
TL;DR: Sketch for a self-serve onboarding wizard and lightweight console/SDK companion that helps customers choose sensible cost/latency/quality presets when first integrating Redwood. Aim: reduce first-month token spend surprises, cut per-token cost by nudging batching/cache/quantization settings, and increase trial->paid conversion by making tradeoffs explicit and reversible.

Context / motivation:
- We see new orgs hitting unexpectedly high token bills in the first weeks. Common causes: long contexts, no batching, always-high-fidelity model variant, no prefix caching.
- Customers (esp. startups) want predictable unit economics and a low-friction way to optimize without deep infra knowledge.
- Our console currently shows post-hoc analytics; we need pre-hoc guidance that plugs into onboarding flows and the SDK.

Goal statement:
- Primary: Provide a 3–5 minute guided experience that outputs a recommended configuration (model variant + batching + cache + token budget per-route) and an SDK snippet + console route to apply it.
- Secondary: Surface estimated cost delta and latency impact for the recommendation vs baseline, and give an A/B quick test harness.

Success metrics (north star + supporting):
- Reduce average new-customer token spend in first 30 days by 20% vs baseline cohort (measured as billed tokens per active user).
- Increase trial->paid conversion by 5% for orgs that complete the wizard.
- % of customers that accept recommended config within 14 days (target 30%).
- Telemetry: median latency change, tokens saved, number of timeouts avoided due to fallback routing when using recommended routing profiles.

Personas:
- Growth/Product engineer at an early-stage startup: cares about cost and iterate speed, wants simple presets and SDK snippet.
- Platform engineer at mid-market: needs to set org defaults and apply to select routes, wants auditing and rollout controls.
- PM evaluating Redwood: needs a readable one-pager showing projected savings for typical workloads.

Non-goals:
- Replace deep performance tuning for Dedicated/private infra. This is an onboarding nudge, not a full optimizer.
- Automatic model switching without user consent.

High-level flow (console + SDK companion):
1) Trigger: new org signs up OR existing org hits 1st billing threshold -> invite to Guided Economy Onramp.
2) Short questionnaire (30–90s):
   - Primary workload type (chat, assistant, summarization, embedding, rerank).
   - Typical context length and distribution (one-box: 0–512 tokens, long-doc: 2–8k, mixed).
   - Latency sensitivity (Interactive <200ms desirable, interactive <500ms ok, batch tolerant).
   - Cost priority (Max quality, Balanced, Min cost).
   - Data sensitivity (sensitive -> avoid hosted-only fallback?)
3) Quick telemetry ingestion: scan sample usage (if org has >1 day usage) to estimate distribution (optional, permissioned).
4) Recommendation engine outputs: preset (Economy / Balanced / Fidelity), model variant (flavor + quantization suggestion), batching config (target batch size, max latency budget), caching hints (prefix caching on/off + TTL), per-route token budget suggestions, and estimated monthly token cost delta.
5) Preview page: single-screen delta summary (savings %, latency impact, risk notes). A/B toggle to create two routes (control + recommended) for canary.
6) One-click apply: implement at org default, or output SDK snippet for a specific route. Provide rollback button and a 7-day auto-revert if key quality regressions reported (opt-in).

User stories (examples):
- As a startup engineer, I want a recommended model + SDK config so I can ship quickly without burning credits.
  Acceptance: Console shows a copy-paste SDK snippet; applying it updates route config and we start seeing telemetry within 5 mins.
- As a platform engineer, I want to apply a preset to a subset of routes so I can control cost for non-critical flows.
  Acceptance: UI supports selecting routes and applying the preset; rollback available per-route.
- As a PM, I want an estimate of monthly savings for my org so I can prioritize adoption.
  Acceptance: Estimate engine uses historical token distribution or default profiles and surfaces a conservative lower bound.

Recommendation logic (sketch):
- Input: questionnaire answers + optional sample usage profile (token length histogram, request rate).
- Rules: map workload to default presets; combine with latency sensitivity to choose batch size and timeout; for long-doc summarization recommend larger models but with prefix trimming and KV cache; for embeddings recommend batched vectorization and chunking.
- Heuristics: if user selects Min cost and latency tolerant -> suggest quantized model variant (e.g., 4-bit), larger batch windows, aggressive prefix caching, and token budget per route. If user selects Fidelity -> recommend fidelity lane, smaller batch size.
- Safety checks: if recommended model is incompatible with private deployment policies or key customer security settings, surface warning and fallback to safer choices.

Telemetry & instrumentation needs:
- Events: onramp_started, questionnaire_completed, recommendation_shown, recommended_applied, revert_triggered, canary_results.
- Metrics: tokens_saved_estimate, actual_tokens_saved, delta_latency_p50/p90, error_rate_delta, conversion_flag.
- Dashboard: per-org card for 30/60 day savings, adoption percent, and quality regressions flagged by eval harness (if enabled).

UX microflow ideas (quick sketches):
- Lightweight modal during signup with progress bar and inline cost estimate.
- Side-by-side comparison: "Current config" vs "Recommended" with colored deltas.
- SDK generator: populate code for JS/Python with feature flags and per-route id examples.
- Inline explainers: short lines (1–2) explaining why each change matters (e.g., "Batching reduces per-token compute by amortizing softmax ops; expect 15–30% cost drop for high-throughput routes").

Rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA):
- MVP (4 weeks): Questionnaire + static mapping to presets + SDK snippet + simple apply to route (console only). Manual review for edge cases.
- Beta (8–12 weeks): Add telemetry ingestion, estimator calibration, canary create & compare, basic auto-revert opt-in, CLI/SDK integration to create programmatic adoption. Invite 50 orgs.
- GA (Q2): Add org-level defaults, audit logs, per-team rollout, and expand recommendations to include quantization profile selection + Dedicated hints.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regressions when pushing lower-fidelity model -> mitigation: require opt-in, show A/B canary, auto-revert and surface eval-run results.
- Overpromising savings -> we present conservative estimates and always show assumptions used (sample size, default token distribution).
- Security/confidentiality -> if org indicates high sensitivity, disable auto-sample ingestion and don't recommend hosted fallbacks.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How to surface cost to seats vs org? Should we expose per-route budget alerts to team leads?
- Acceptance conditions for auto-revert: what thresholds of quality drop (semantic eval) should trigger revert? (talk to Applied ML/Evals) @Mika Sato
- Data retention/consent flow for optional usage profile ingestion (legal input needed).
- Backend: do we build recommendation engine as a stateless microservice or piggyback on Optimize? Estimate infra cost and cache results per-org.
- Product: microcopy & examples — need 3 concrete workspace types for the questionnaire (chatbot, docs assistant, nightly batch summarizer).

Short TODO list:
- [ ] Sync with Applied ML on quantization guidance and safety (owner: Mika)
- [ ] Draft SDK snippet templates for JS/Python and small README (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Spike estimator using sampled data from 10 trial orgs (owner: Harper)
- [ ] Legal review for telemetry ingestion consent copy (owner: Nadia)
- [ ] Initial console mockups (1-screen & modal) — link Figma when ready

Notes to self: keep defaults conservative, surface assumptions prominently, and make rollback trivial. Target demo for leadership: show a real org where we reduce token spend 30% with <2% measurable quality loss (if any).

Slack refs: #product-hosted-api (thread: guided-econ-idea) and ping @Mika for ML boundary checks.

-- end of scratchpad (lots to refine but this is the scaffolding).
